quotations.text: This image of alchemical marriage was used by several alchemists

claims.sentence_start: Copy-text Farmer 1998
Akopyan and Mandosio quote the same words
'magicam' is the accusative
'maritare' is the vinedresser's verb
claims.note: Oration: 'Et sicut agricola ulmos vitibus, ita magus terram caelo ... maritat'; Copenhaver: 'as a farmer marries elm to vine'.

claims.sentence_start: Pico's own opinion: the thirteenth magical conclusion
Oration: 'Et sicut agricola ulmos vitibus'
Plotinus, Enneads 4.4.40
claims.note: Copenhaver n. 9 (24165): 'Plot. Enn. 4.4.40-45, esp. 40.9-19'. Note that Copenhaver's 'axiom' (17502-17509) is the principle that the magus serves nature as she works; the love-drawing passage then leads into the marriage image.

claims.sentence_start: Virgil, Georgics; Horace, Epodes 2.9-10; Ovid
The thesis defines the whole of magical operation
Farmer reads 9>10-14 as one series
The same series joins the idea of man as microcosm
On this reading the purified magus receives the power
The Oration spells the image out
Magic in this sense does not make its effects
Copenhaver traces the axiom to Plotinus
claims.note: Copenhaver's 'axiom' is the serving-nature principle quoted at 17502-17509; the Plotinus passage he then quotes is the love-drawing one, as the sentence says. Supported, with that caveat about the word 'axiom'.

claims.sentence_start: Pico, he writes, turned this into plainer words
claims.note: First half supported ('In Pico's plainer words—with help from Roman poets—"as a farmer marries elm to vine..."'). The second half reverses Copenhaver: 'Nuptializing this vineyard image, he picked the theme up from one of his theses: T2M13', i.e. the Oration's image takes the theme from 9>13; Copenhaver does not say that the thesis took the theme up from the image.

claims.sentence_start: He points to Ovid's Vertumnus
Mandosio makes the marriage of the world
claims.note: 'the "marriage of the world", which is the scope of the magical work—that is, to unite what is above (supercelestial entities) to what is below (corporeal things)'.

claims.sentence_start: Mandosio argues that for Pico the magus
claims.note: Mandosio: he 'needs cabalistic skills in order to be able to attract the divine emanations (the sefirot or numerationes) and direct their influence towards the physical world' (515-517). He does not tie this to 9>15; the link is the drafter's.

claims.sentence_start: Akopyan reads the image as an alchemical marriage
claims.note: 2018 n. 47: 'This image of alchemical marriage was used by several alchemists and has become popular thanks to Carl Gustav Jung.' 2021: 'compares the harmony of the knowledge of the world with a marriage (probably by analogy with the alchemical arts)'.

claims.sentence_start: Ebgi uses the same verb
claims.note: Entry CHARACTERES, signed [R. E.] at 10199: conventional scripts are 'incapaci cioè di maritare il mondo delle cose a quello del pensiero'.

claims.sentence_start: Farmer's reading is eschatological
He sets this reading of the magus as cosmic priest against Yates
Busi reads the thesis anthropologically
claims.note: Busi: 'Quasi fosse un consumato sensale del cosmo, il mago pichiano ricongiunge ciò che è spaiato, celebra le nozze della materia, e unisce ieraticamente maschio e femmina'. The content is supported; 'anthropologically' is the drafter's label and does not fit (Busi's frame at 1538-1540 is restoring the whole to its primal integrity).

claims.sentence_start: Copenhaver's contribution is philological
claims.note: He does identify Plotinus and the Roman poets; calling his contribution 'philological' is an editorial characterisation.

claims.sentence_start: The disagreement is over what is married
claims.note: Declared editorial comparison. 'matter paired with matter for Busi' simplifies Busi, who also speaks of rejoining male and female and restoring the whole to its integrity (1538-1543).

claims.sentence_start: Whether Pico had any alchemical source in view

translation.note: 'Magicam operari non est aliud quam maritare mundum' (farmer1998:25280); Farmer's English (25322) has the same sense. 'wed' for 'maritare' keeps the nuptial sense; 'nothing else than' keeps 'non est aliud quam'.

note: One NOT SUPPORTED clause (Copenhaver's direction of borrowing reversed) removed; one drafter's link (to 9>15) removed; the label 'anthropologically' replaced by the neutral 'thus' (a removal of the label).
